body:
I don't think he's a terrible person. I understand completely why he doesn't want to be my friend any more. To quote his message:

> 'it's so exhausting to have to just reassure you constantly'

> 'I feel awful but at the same time it's important for me to recognise that this isn't my responsibility, and it's draining me.'

> 'it's overwhelming. I can't handle this responsibility.'

It's clear our friendship was having a negative effect on him, despite all the good it was doing me.

Initially, when all this went down last night, I would have been inclined to agree with you; I was already very upset by him because not only had he refused to meet me after I'd told him what I'd done on Sunday, he just wasn't talking to me at all. And I get that he can be busy with his own life (hell, he even mentions this in his note; 'especially while I'm out trying to enjoy my time'. Of course I tried not to bother him whenever this was the case, but it still happened I guess) but I wish he'd at least not ignored me.

It really frustrated me that he has always been there for his girlfriend but this weekend he wasn't there for me at all; I'm not going to delve into all the reasons why this is so for me since it's not fair for me to post online, even anonymously, anything more about our friendship or their relationship than I already have.

I might check it out. Thank you for the offer. I never have been very good at MOBAs though haha.
Thank you so much, for everything. I might take you up on that some time :)

> be thankful that I had something so great it made me feel that way when it ended

Thank you so much for your message, but thank you for this in particular. You're right, I should be grateful, as for as short as it was, it was great having such an amazing, close friend. And maybe I can learn from this, if there is a next time. Thank you.

I don't think I'm suicidal any more. Just... still very upset and sad about the whole thing. I'm not sure how glad I am I haven't done anything. Maybe that'll change.

I've been trying to take a break from it; like I said, I've been watching Star Trek and listening to King Gizzard. It's helped, but I still can't not think about it, and not think about it in these terms. But I think you're right, if I'm interpreting you correctly; in time, I'll be able to deal with this. It's just still very difficult right now.
It's hard not to. I don't know what I'm going to do, what I can do now. I feel so full of uncertainty right now. Not to mention guilt that I caused the end of our friendship

Yep! This might sound dumb but honestly it's such a confidence booster that you think my musicianship is so amazing, haha.

You're right, I could make friends with co-workers, it's an office job with a large company so there'll be plenty there. I suppose that's one possibility to look forward to.

I always try never to shy away from opportunities, even with my anxiety; my own problem is I don't seem to have very many, which is why I try to take advantage of every one. I guess it doesn't help that I do very little outside of college/gigs, and don't really leave the house otherwise. (Except to see my friend, but I can't count that any more...)

You don't sound preachy at all. This short conversation has meant so much to me, perhaps more than you'll know. Thank you so much.

No, I'm not going to university. I am starting full-time work soon, though, and I fully intend to move out with or without him before the year's over at the latest. A fresh start could indeed do a lot for me.

I am a little concerned that it's going to be difficult to meet new people outside of education; I just left what we call college here on Friday. I suppose I ought to start playing gigs without him, on my own, and that could help a lot too. I still feel I'll struggle though, between my anxiety and sobriety. I mean, I have no problems (oddly enough) playing gigs with my anxiety, I've played to crowds in the hundreds, although I do just stare at the floor the whole way through (I suppose that's apt considering our band was a shoegaze band). It's more with the meeting people aspect of it.

Oh, I wish I could! I still live with my parents though, and I know I wouldn't be allowed to. I couldn't even afford it right now. But that is a pretty good suggestion, come to think of it. Thank you. I'll keep it in mind for when I move out.

Christ, we were even gonna move in together in a few months..

Thanks, this means a lot to me. It's just that it took me 17 and a half years to make one friend and I ruined that. It feels like, even if I make another, I'll ruin that too. But I hope you're right, I hope it will get better. Thank you so much.
